1.explanation: TableToolbarMenu.js is the component that wraps Carbon’s OverflowMenu and applies the toolbar menu styling. It currently passes the `iconDescription` value into the `title` prop of OverflowMenu but does not map it to the `ariaLabel` prop. As a result, OverflowMenu falls back to its default aria‐label (“Menu”), which doesn’t match the visible label (“Settings”) and causes the 2.5.3 violation. By updating TableToolbarMenu to forward `iconDescription` to `ariaLabel`, the ARIA name and visible label will match, resolving the violation.
1.bug_scenario: The issue is an IBM 2.5.3 “Label in Name” violation in the DataTable’s toolbar overflow menu button. If you look at the screenshot, the toolbar renders a gear‐icon button (the “Settings” menu) with a title attribute of “Settings,” yet the button’s aria‐label is coming through as “Menu.” That mismatch between the visible label (the gear icon labeled “Settings”) and the accessible name (“Menu”) triggers the violation.
